scope: Deployment capability CLI and workstation fast/A-B transport hold lifecycle. The managed-image guard still prohibits legacy unsigned A/B installation.

validation.suite_note: The full Python suite preceded final JS confirmation/reconnect refinements; the final full Node suite includes them. Rust production source was unchanged after the 58-case host and Pi checks. ARM binaries were stripped for transfer. No packaged image was rebuilt.

contracts.capability_transport: stdin only, one newline-terminated line; never command arguments or environment

properties_exercised: Capabilities are bounded/redacted on stdin, and the real CLI rejects malformed input before contacting the service on the host and both Pis.

Mode Off admits a persisted deployment reservation without enabling an independently off radio or claiming a working link. Turning the policy on later preserves that hold. Unresolved radio commands still block admission.
The existing real-process hold ownership, persisted deployment, reboot grace and interrupted-radio fixtures remain passing; deployment was added to the hold-during-shutdown/restoration comparison.
The workstation reuses one capability through command gaps, heartbeat renewal and reboot. A service that appears after a legacy-image reboot is admitted before validation continues.

Unavailable/malformed policy cannot select legacy fallback. Lost admission responses still attempt release. Admission failure prevents staging/transfer; failed renewal after transfer prevents installer launch while preserving cleanup/release order.

Renewal continues during long work. Failure does not interrupt an installer, but subsequent steps require fresh acknowledgement. Expected reboot outages are tolerated, and reconnect retries must obtain acknowledgement before success.

A/B confirmation occurs before final admission and no longer exits inside the legacy helper on cancellation. Cancellation, failed transfer/checksum/flash and missed reboot cannot print update completion and still leave the hold cleanup path.
Captured SSH output and process duration are bounded, remote stderr is not echoed with secret input, and release failure cannot replace the original install error.
The managed-image guard continues rejecting unsigned A/B installation. Tests use fake SSH/transfers/flash/reboot, and physical Pis run only private fixtures and malformed-input CLI checks.

limits: No physical update, installed service change, real lease admission, radio toggle, boot/root/data partition change or watchdog operation was performed. Boot IDs stayed unchanged during each Pi run.

Fast update hold integration has not yet been qualified against an installed native coordinator during an actual transfer/restart/rollback. Root operator access and matching image rollout remain pending.

The A/B wrapper is tested with injected transport/reboot fixtures. The public managed path remains deliberately blocked until the verified workstation installer is integrated; these tests do not prove a signed root installation or physical reboot recovery.

Heartbeat/reconnect command bounds rely on the SSH child exiting after termination; an uninterruptible OS process is outside this fixture qualification. The root service independently bounds its persisted lease and live-operation checks.

Workstation process termination can leave the persisted lease for bounded expiry. Kiosk restarts do not finish that transaction. No claim is made that a killed workstation can recover its in-memory capability.
Expected setup profile coordination, native SSH idle qualification, daily synchronization, production signing/feed, downloader/install policy and full hardware OTA qualification remain unfinished.
